Hi, I have recently made some really clear bright holos with the Colourgraphics BB-640 plates. After a few days the plates have a dark brown appearance and the holo looks a little darker.

I would like to know,

1. It it exposure to DIRECT sunlight that causes this?

2. Is it exposure to light in general that causes this.

3. I have tried re bleaching for 30 seconds - this seams to have cleared the brown colour, and kept the image intact. - will the brown come back on exposure to sunlight?

P.S. I really would recommend these plates over PFG-03m

Thanks for any advise, Rick.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
I assume you are using a rehalogenating bleach such as ferric EDTA? Anyway, a treatment which greatly reduces printout is a final rinse in a mild (1%) acetic acid bath before squeegeeing and drying. This leaves a slightly acid environment which inhibits redevelopment, and someone also claimed that it dissolved the sensitizing dyes (not sure about that).

Cheap white vinegar is totally inorganic - it is 4-5% pure acetic acid (derived from acetylene gas) and can be used when diluted down to 1%. The vinegar makes squeegeeing more difficult (the rubber blade doesn't slide smoothly and squeaks) but don't use a wetting agent like PhotoFlow - it has been implicated in printout and doesn't work with vinegar anyway.

It's been a long time since I did sunlight tests - why not try the treatment on half of a plate, let it sit in direct sun for a few hours and report back on the results?

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md: I had this same problem many years ago. Re-bleaching did remove the problem, but it just occurred again. My solution was to use a stop bath between the developer and bleach. You can go directly from the developer to the stop bath without washing and keep it in the bath for 2 minutes with agitation. I use Kodak's Indicator Stop bath with a 32:1 ratio of distilled water to stop bath solution (mixing directions are on the stop bath container). After the stop bath, I wash in running water for 5 minutes, then bleach. This approach essentially gives the hologram archival properties. Since using this approach, I've never had a hologram of any type of emulsion or developed in any type of developer turn brown on me again, even in bright sunlight.

did you use the recommended Pyrogallol developer process? As far as I know, if you use reversal bleach ("Pyrochrome processing"), the Holos are not affected by print out in sunlight at all. (according to the "Holofibel" by Peter Heiß, German). But I dont know yet about print out effects after Ferric EDTA-Bleaching.
